calls.head: Forecheck against patience
calls.body: On forecheck pressure, Carolina is one of the league’s best, but Chicago is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Expect the Hurricanes to win more pucks back deep in the Blackhawks’ end.

surprises.head: Chicago hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: Chicago is one of the league’s lightest-hitting teams. Even by those standards, this was a quiet night on the body: a hit score of 27 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 76 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 20 games.

story.head: The Hurricanes beat the Blackhawks
paras: Mark Jankowski struck first for the Hurricanes late in the first. It was a busy second period. Sebastian Aho and Jackson Blake scored a little over a minute apart early in the period to stretch the lead to 3-0. Roman Kantserov, in his sixth NHL game, scored his first NHL goal a little over a minute later to get the Blackhawks on the board. Taylor Hall stretched the lead to 4-1 a minute and a half later, and Jordan Martinook made it 5-1 early in the third. Oliver Moore made a dent in Carolina’s lead late in the period, bringing it to 5-2.

The Hurricanes carried the play, outshooting the Blackhawks 39-26, and got the result to match. Brandon Bussi made 24 saves for the Canes, and Spencer Knight allowed five goals on 39 shots. The Hurricanes improved to 4-1-1, and the Blackhawks dropped to 1-5-0.

items.text: Four straight wins for the Hurricanes.
Sebastian Aho has a point in five straight games.
Jordan Martinook scored his first goal of the season, his first since Apr 2 (ten games played since).
One of the preview’s two calls held.
